payload.scores:
Scored against the five criteria from derive_criteria; the datum is today's behaviour. Scale: veto criteria pass or fail, the rest -1 / 0 / +1 against the datum.

DATUM - merge everything, no tag, no branch commits: C1 nothing-lost FAIL (an empty branch closes as success and its work is never committed anywhere); C2 trunk-clean -1 (57 evidence files per close); C3 permanent name FAIL (no tag exists); C4 no partial state 0 (a conflict does abort today); C5 ordinary mechanics +1.

CHOSEN - 1a+2a+3a+4a+5a: C1 PASS (probed: evidence readable from the tag after the close, and milestone commits mean the branch holds the work even if the close never runs); C2 +1 (probed: trunk tree carries only claims); C3 PASS (tag created before the merge, refusal if it cannot be); C4 +1 (every failure path refuses and leaves trunk untouched); C5 +1 (merge, rm --cached, commit - plain git, and the repository stays comprehensible without SE).

Metrics from the partitioning: four clusters, one standing constraint; the only inter-cluster interface is the tag name, which is deterministic (iter/<id>) and therefore needs no coordination between the bless path and the close path. Coupling count between A/C and B is zero, which is what allows the close to refuse without undoing committed milestones.

EXAMPLES EXERCISED against the chosen combination: UC-A main scenario walks as probes A2-A5; UC-A ext 1a as probe A1; UC-C as probe A5 (a path resolved out of the tag); UC-A composition across iterations as probe A6. UC-B and UC-D are not yet exercised - they are build-time checks, and that gap is named rather than papered over.
payload.front: The surviving set is a single point: 1a+2a+3a+4a+5a. It dominates the datum on every criterion where they differ and ties on none that matter. No second non-dominated candidate exists, because every alternative enumerated fails either a veto criterion (1c, 1d, 4b breach nothing-lost or the invariant), the binding scope (5c is i5e), or ordinary-mechanics (1b, 2c, 3b, 3c). A Pareto front of one is recorded as exactly that - not disguised as a comparison.
payload.eliminations: 1b build the tree by hand - dominated on C5, identical result with more machinery. 1c merge-then-delete-after - fails C2 as an invariant: a checkout of the intermediate commit still contains the events, so trunk would be clean only eventually. 1d merge -s ours plus selective checkout - fails C1: it inverts the default so an unlisted CLAIM is silently dropped, and losing a claim is worse than leaking an event. 2b frontmatter classification - cannot cover JSON evidence runs, so it fails to classify the heavy material at all. 2c per-iteration configuration - makes the invariant negotiable, which is erosion by design. 3b commit per submit - granularity far below a milestone, buries the branch history. 3c commit on a timer - unrelated to any process boundary. 4b tag after the merge - leaves a window in which events are out of the tree and unnamed, breaching R1's mitigation. 4c tag at open - the tag would need moving later, and moving a published tag is the history mutation R11 forbids in spirit. 5b stub directories - reintroduces the clutter being removed. 5c read from tags now - out of the binding scope, it is i5e.
